title: mini sprint kernel todo - Carmen Li
content:
Daily mini-sprint scratchpad (fast, noisy, action-first)
Owner: Carmen Li — focused kernel/kv-cache micro-tasks before EOD.

MORNING TRIAGE (09:00)
- Observed: p99 token latency spike across small models (sequence 512) on rtx-dedicated nodes. Spike correlates with KV cache evictions (see kibana: trace id 8f3b).
- Quick reproducer: run local client against dev cluster with --seq=512 --parallel=8; pattern: tail latency jumps after ~20k tokens.
  $ ./bench --model=redwood-small --seq=512 --clients=8 --duration=120s
  Look at /metrics/kv/cache_evictions and /metrics/serve/tokens_per_sec.

HYPOTHESIS
- Hot prefix churn is causing frequent KV invalidation because current prefix hashing doesn't account for truncated-system prompts. Eviction thrash + small batch sizes -> increased kernel context rebuilds.

QUICK ACTIONS (priority order)
1) Patch small workaround on dev: increase kv.max_entries_per_shard from 16k to 32k to see if eviction rate drops. (Low-risk, perf config change). Track evictions and p99 for 2h. -> TODO: Arjun to deploy config change (JIRA-4521).
2) Add quick metric: kv.eviction_reason{reason="prefix-truncation"} — instrument where we drop based on prefix len. Minimal patch in runtime-handler, compile and smoke test. -> TODO: Carmen + Lena pair for 1.5h.
3) Experiment with batching window: increase micro-batch window from 8ms -> 15ms on canary to absorb bursts. Measure token throughput delta and tail latency. If throughput loss <3% and p99 improves -> consider gradual rollout. -> TODO: myself to queue canary.
4) Short-term fallback: route greedy low-cost requests to quantized-variant (v1-q4) when queue depth > 24. Implement route rule in smart-routing config for today only (manual rollout).

REPRO STEPS / DEBUG NOTES
- Reproducer flagging: set env DEBUG_KV=1 on one shard and tail logs to catch exact key length when eviction triggered.
- Kernel SIGUSR1 handler already dumps active KV size; add small timestamp to logs so we can correlate with trace ids.
- When capturing heap profile: run pmap + jemalloc stats every 60s during experiment.

SMALL PATCH PLAN (20m each)
- Patch A: increase shard cap config (no code change) -> validate in staging -> deploy to dev.
- Patch B: tiny metric + log: add "eviction_reason" label, increment on path where we drop by prefix rules.
- Patch C: batching window knob make runtime-config-overridable per-route (adds config path only).

METRICS TO COLLECT (for acceptance)
- kv.evictions_total (rate), kv.entries_per_shard (gauge), serve.latency.p99_ms (by model, seq), tokens/sec (aggregate), batch.size.histogram.
- Baseline before changes (snapshot saved to S3: s3://redwood-dev/experiments/2024-11-05/baseline.json).

RISKS / NOTES
- Increasing shard capacity increases memory footprint. Must keep per-GPU mem delta < 8% otherwise OOM risk on smaller machines. Add mem gauge in canary.
- Longer batching window increases latency for single-request tail; we only apply to models with sequence >=256 for canary.

AFTERNOON CHECKPOINT (15:00)
- If eviction rate drops >40% and p99 improves -> promote config to 50% of dev fleet. If mem delta >6% -> rollback and try alternative (eviction smarter rule).

OPEN QUESTIONS (short list)
- Is prefix-truncation eviction the real culprit or a correlated symptom? How common are long-system prompts in production? (ask product for sample prompt histogram).
- Could we do a cheap bloom-filter style pre-check to reduce unnecessary inserts? Prototype cost?

EXPERIMENTAL IDEAS (longer-term)
- Adaptive shard sizing: track per-shard hotness and temporarily expand shard budget for heavy prefixes. Requires safe resizing in-place.
- Prioritized KV retention: keep entries that are referenced in last 10s while demoting one-shot prefixes.

EOD TODO (quick list)
- [ ] Arjun: deploy shard cap bump to dev + post metrics in JIRA-4521.
- [ ] Carmen+Lena: implement eviction_reason metric + small log change (PR draft).
- [ ] Carmen: queue canary route change for batching window and monitor 2h.
- [ ] Ping product for prompt histogram sample (ask in slack #prod-data).
- [ ] Write short note for next standup summarizing outcome and next steps.

RANDOM NOTES / micro-ideas
- Consider adding a "kv.hot_prefixes" small cache for top-100 prefixes per-shard (eviction: LRU). Cheap if keys are short.
- If we can safely quantize KV entries (compress keys) maybe reduce footprint; need to verify lookup cost.

END — quick status to drop in #runtime-triage after first canary results.
